# AP-BOOTSTRAP-1 PCM conformance vectors

**Generated by `make_vectors.c`. Do not edit by hand.**

Every file is 48 kHz monaural signed 16-bit PCM, and every one is a
complete `AP-BOOTSTRAP-1` transmission as `spec/ap-bootstrap-1.md`
describes it -- 0.1 s of silence, a 0.2 s chirp, 16 training symbols,
a 3-byte PHY header, the payload, and trailing silence.

## How to use these

A receiver is conformant against this corpus when it recovers the
stated payload from every `accept` vector and produces the stated
refusal for every `refuse` vector. **The refusals carry the weight.**
A receiver that accepts everything passes all three positive vectors
and is not a receiver.

The expected refusals distinguish *heard nothing* from *heard
something and could not read it*. Those are different problems with
the same shape, and only the second means a link is nearly working, so
an implementation that collapses them into one failure is not
conformant even though it rejects the right files.

| Vector | Expected | Payload | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `01-presence-10b.wav` | accept | `10020A11EDC00000043C` | the 10-byte first-contact announcement |
| `02-transport-accept-16b.wav` | accept | `180A0A11EDC000C0FFEE03010D0C0DE5` | the 16-byte reply |
| `03-transport-offer-17b.wav` | accept | `18020A11EDC000C0FFEE03015E1EC7ED3C` | the 17-byte offer, the largest object in the sequence |
| `04-refuse-bad-crc.wav` | refuse: CRC | `-` | a valid PRESENCE whose header CRC is inverted |
| `05-refuse-zero-length.wav` | refuse: payload | `-` | declared length 0, which names no payload |
| `06-refuse-length-over-cap.wav` | refuse: payload | `-` | declared length 200, above the 64-byte cap; a receiver must reject this **before** reading 200 bytes |
| `07-refuse-truncated.wav` | refuse: sync | `-` | cut off inside the payload, as an interrupted transmission is |
| `08-refuse-no-preamble.wav` | refuse: not acquired | `-` | a complete, correct frame with no chirp in front of it |
| `09-refuse-silence.wav` | refuse: not acquired | `-` | two seconds of digital silence |

## What these vectors do not cover

They are **noise-free**. Every one is the transmitter's own output,
so they test that a receiver reads the format correctly and say
nothing about whether it works over air. The over-air evidence is
`experiments/011-bootstrap-over-air/`, and the two are not
substitutes: a receiver can pass every vector here and still fail in
a room, because the thing that fails in a room is timing recovery
and these vectors have perfect timing.

In particular **nothing here exercises the whole-frame rate
refinement that §6.4 makes mandatory**, because these frames decode on
the first attempt. A receiver that omitted §6.4 entirely would pass
this corpus. That is a known limit of noise-free vectors and is the
reason §11 requires a clean-room receiver tested against captures as
well as against these.
